Dis the Dis Information Website Case Study

Project Overview:
Dis the Dis aimed to challenge the negative perceptions associated with the label of being disabled. The founders wanted to launch an information website to establish credibility and be taken seriously by investors, partners, and collaborators.

Lean Methodology:
Our approach for this project was a lean methodology, consisting of a discovery call with the clients, asynchronous empathic journey mapping, website information architecture mapping, and UI design. The goal was to cut down long pieces of text and convey the information in an impactful and non-overwhelming way that is easy to skim and navigate.

Discovery Call:
We conducted a discovery call with the founders of Dis the Dis to gather information about their goals and objectives for the website. During this call, we discussed their target audience, brand identity, and key messaging.

Empathic Journey Mapping:
We conducted asynchronous empathic journey mapping to understand the users' experience and identify pain points. This helped us to optimize the user experience and provide a seamless flow for users to access the information they needed.

Website Information Architecture:
We mapped the website's information architecture to ensure that it was intuitive and easy to navigate. This helped us to organize the information in a logical way and make sure that users could find what they were looking for quickly and easily.

UI Design:
The final UIs were designed with the user in mind, ensuring an intuitive and user-friendly experience. We aimed to simplify the design and focus on conveying the information in an impactful way that was easy to skim and navigate.

Outcome:
The Dis the Dis information website was a success and received positive feedback from users. The website effectively communicated the mission of Dis the Dis and its goals in a simple and non-overwhelming way. The project demonstrates our ability to approach projects with a lean methodology and develop effective solutions that meet the client's requirements.

In their first year they wanted to launch by holding pirate days and schools that aimed to spread empathic awareness around disability in children, the website provided information and resources for schools to run these events as well as feedback forms.

Project Overview: Dis the Dis Information Website

Dis the Dis aimed to challenge negative perceptions associated with being disabled and promote empathy towards those with disabilities. In their first year, Dis the Dis planned to launch Pirate Days in schools to spread empathic awareness about disability in children. The goal of the Dis the Dis information website was to communicate what the startup was about and convey its future goals. The website provided information and resources for schools to run the Pirate Days and included feedback forms for users to provide input. The website was designed to be a central hub for all information related to the Dis the Dis mission.

Write a sentence about the goal of the discovery that demonstrates to the user how we become obsessed with the clients vision and goals for the project by giving them a chance to share, and for us to listen.

The goal of the discovery phase was to immerse ourselves in the client's vision and goals for the project, giving them a platform to share and us the opportunity to listen intently, resulting in a deep understanding and commitment to delivering a solution that exceeded their expectations.
Can you rewrite that in fewer words

The discovery phase aimed to understand the client's vision and goals thoroughly by listening to their perspectives and becoming deeply invested in delivering a solution that exceeds their expectations.

proposal.summary: Created two local memory entries capturing user-verified facts about the Dis the Dis information website project and the user's client-services design practice.
proposal.rationale: The user directly reported (m_0002:0) the corrected project facts for Dis the Dis: the website's goal was to communicate what the startup is about and convey future goals, with first-year launch via Pirate Days at schools to spread empathic awareness around disability in children, providing schools event resources and feedback forms. This supersedes the earlier assistant-drafted framing (investor credibility), which is excluded as an unsupported assistant claim. The user also stated (m_0004:0) that they work on client projects ('we', 'the clients vision') with a discovery process centered on listening to and becoming invested in the client's vision. Both are durable, host-neutral facts with direct user evidence and no existing harness coverage; assistant-only methodology details (lean approach, journey mapping, IA mapping) were excluded per evidence rules.

edits.title: Dis the Dis information website: communicate startup mission and first-year Pirate Days school events (reported 2023-09-11)
edits.content: Dis the Dis is a startup that challenges negative perceptions associated with being disabled. The goal of the Dis the Dis information website was to communicate what Dis the Dis was about and convey the startup's future goals. In their first year, the startup planned to launch by holding Pirate Days at schools aimed at spreading empathic awareness around disability in children; the website provided information and resources for schools to run these events, as well as feedback forms. This user-provided description supersedes an earlier draft framing that the website's goal was to establish credibility with investors, partners, and collaborators.
edits.reason: The user explicitly corrected the project overview with these facts; no prior harness entry covers Dis the Dis, and recording the user-stated purpose prevents future reliance on the superseded assistant framing.

edits.title: User's team delivers client website projects; discovery phase centers on listening to the client's vision (stated 2023-09-11)
edits.content: The user works on client website projects as part of a team; the founders of Dis the Dis were clients. Their discovery process is built around giving clients a chance to share while the team listens and becomes deeply invested in (described by the user as becoming 'obsessed' with) the client's vision and goals for the project. Stated 2023-09-11 while refining the Dis the Dis case study copy.
edits.reason: Direct user evidence establishes the user's client-services project context and discovery philosophy, which is durable, host-neutral, and useful for interpreting future project and case-study requests.
